name: Magna Carta design tokens
description: Resolver for the Magna Carta design-token source: primitive ramps + semantic aliases (the light/default truth), modified by theme and mode. Mode overlays re-point semantic aliases to ramp positions and are shared across all themes; a new theme adds one context that swaps ramp values only.

primitives.description: Primitive scales: color ramps, dimensions, typography, shadows, z-index, motion.

semantic.description: Semantic aliases onto primitives; the only names components consume.

theme.description: Visual theme (firm-picked). chancery is the flagship default (Ink & Gold, baked into the primitives); each showcase theme adds one context that swaps the neutral+brand ramp VALUES only. The shared accent (gold) and status ramps never vary by theme.

mode.description: Light or dark color mode, shared across all themes. Light is empty: tokens/semantic.json is the light/default truth. Dark re-points color-bearing semantic aliases to other ramp positions.

density.description: The user density axis (design language §5: comfortable / compact). comfortable is the semantic truth; compact re-points the density.* aliases ONLY (dimensions are theme- and mode-invariant), emitted as one small :root[data-density=…] overlay block after the theme x mode permutations. Recipes consume control heights and row geometry exclusively through density.* — that consumption IS the axis compliance.

motion.description: The user motion axis (design language §7: full / reduced / off, honoring OS prefers-reduced-motion as the default). full is the primitive truth; reduced/off re-point the duration ladder ONLY (durations are theme- and mode-invariant), emitted as small :root[data-motion=…] overlay blocks AFTER the theme x mode permutations so they win the duration variables at equal specificity. Recipes never gate themselves — referencing the ladder IS the compliance.

typeface.description: The user typeface axis (design language: the reading font is a user accessibility choice — Atkinson Hyperlegible Next by default, Lexend, OpenDyslexic, a serif reading profile, or the system face). atkinson is the primitive truth; each other context re-points font.sans ONLY (a font stack is theme-, mode- and density-invariant), emitted as one small :root[data-typeface=…] overlay block after the theme x mode permutations so it wins the variable at equal specificity. Recipes read the reading face through var(--mc-font-sans) — that consumption IS the axis compliance.

contrast.description: Reserved high-contrast axis (design language §6; the home for stronger boundaries + OS prefers-contrast / forced-colors). Unpopulated at launch — only the no-op 'standard' context exists; a future 'high' context strengthens borders and drops subtle shadows. The plugin permutations (terrazzo.config.mjs) emit theme x mode only, so this resolves to its default and adds no output until populated.
